method: Static read-only inspection of pre-existing shallow clones. No repository code, installers, package lifecycle scripts, hooks, MCP servers, or tests were executed.

sources.name: graphify
sources.recommendation: Keep disabled by default; use only for repository-relationship and architecture questions. Run in the workspace and keep generated graph output outside prompt startup context.
permissions_and_behavior: Core CLI reads source trees and writes graph/cache output; cache cleanup deletes only its cache entries.
Optional MCP, database, file-watcher, cloud-LLM, office, video, and graph-export extras add network, credential, filesystem, or service access.
Query logging is opt-in; when enabled it can write query and optionally response data to a log path.
credentials_network_telemetry: Optional OpenAI, Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini, Neo4j, FalkorDB, and Google integrations require their normal external configuration.
No automatic telemetry was identified in the inspected core; query logging is explicitly opt-in.
sources.tests_and_docs: pytest configuration targets tests; README and packaged host-specific skill files exist. Static inspection cannot confirm documentation/runtime parity.
evidence: pyproject.toml:5-12,51-88 (license, optional services, MCP and CLI entry points)

sources.name: serena
sources.recommendation: Do not enable by default. If approved, constrain it to the workspace, review available editing/shell tools, and require explicit user approval for shell or write operations.
permissions_and_behavior: The MCP-oriented toolkit exposes semantic retrieval and editing capabilities.
File tools include create/replace/line-edit operations that write project files.
Its shell helper uses subprocess.Popen with shell=True and inherits an environment copy.
credentials_network_telemetry: Dependencies include requests, python-dotenv, MCP, Anthropic, and optional Google integrations.
The inspected manifest is broadly pinned, but the access surface still includes filesystem mutation, processes, and optional network-backed providers.
sources.tests_and_docs: pytest, lint, and type-check tasks are defined; README and MCP server script are present. No test or server was run.
evidence: pyproject.toml:5-55,64-70,72-101,164-175 (MCP/CLI, pinned dependencies, optional providers, test/lint tasks)
src/serena/util/shell.py:16-49 (shell command execution; shell=True at line 30)

sources.name: context7
sources.recommendation: Treat as an optional, approved external documentation service. Do not auto-configure its remote MCP endpoint or credentials; use only when current version-specific external documentation is needed.
permissions_and_behavior: The Codex plugin config points to an HTTPS MCP endpoint rather than a local-only process.
The MCP package registers tools and supports OAuth discovery/auth flow.
CLI tracking posts events to a remote API; the monorepo and MCP packaging scripts contain destructive node_modules cleanup and install/build steps that were not executed.
credentials_network_telemetry: A CONTEXT7_API_KEY is documented for higher quotas.
Remote MCP URL and CLI event tracking create network and telemetry exposure.
sources.tests_and_docs: Root and MCP package define pnpm tests and package documentation; lockfile exists. No package lifecycle or test command was run.
evidence: packages/mcp/src/index.ts:112-264,501-631 (MCP server, tool registration, OAuth discovery)

sources.name: repomix
sources.recommendation: Keep optional and use only with explicit include/exclude filters for bounded handoffs. Do not activate its MCP server by default or run lifecycle/install scripts without a separate review.
permissions_and_behavior: The tool packages repository content into output files and includes MCP tools for local file reads, directory reads, output attachment, and remote repository packing.
Package prepare automatically builds when npm lifecycle scripts are allowed; build removes lib before compiling.
Remote repository and watch/MCP features expand network or filesystem exposure beyond a simple filtered export.
credentials_network_telemetry: MCP registration includes remote-repository packing and filesystem read tools.
No core telemetry conclusion is made from the static scan; website analytics is separate from the CLI/MCP review.
sources.tests_and_docs: vitest and secretlint scripts are defined; README and MCP source are present. No build, prepare, MCP, or test execution occurred.

sources.name: aider
sources.recommendation: Keep separate from this agent platform. Use only when Aider is the explicitly selected coding client, with a separate credential and command-execution review.
permissions_and_behavior: Terminal coding client can run shell commands through a helper that invokes subprocess.Popen with shell=True.
Analytics integrates PostHog, writes a user-home analytics file, supports custom endpoint/key overrides, and has disable controls.
The codebase supports many model/provider credentials and repository-editing workflows; it must not be treated as a passive portable skill.
credentials_network_telemetry: Analytics code contains a PostHog host/project key and can post events when enabled.
Provider configuration uses environment-backed credentials; do not expose them to an agent extension.
sources.tests_and_docs: Dynamic dependency files and documentation are present; tests include analytics coverage. No installer, model call, shell command, or test was executed.
evidence: pyproject.toml:2-49 (Apache license classifier, CLI entry point, dynamic dependency files)
aider/analytics.py:56-105,137-183,213-250 (PostHog, local analytics persistence, event handling)

sources.name: code-review-graph
sources.recommendation: Disabled by default and never active alongside Graphify without benchmark evidence. Do not adopt its MCP config or automatic hooks; use only after explicit approval and narrow workspace confinement.
permissions_and_behavior: The supplied MCP config launches uvx code-review-graph serve, which can install/run an external package at activation time.
Supplied SessionStart/PostToolUse hooks invoke status, background build, and update commands automatically.
The FastMCP server registers many tools, including graph build/update and query operations; daemon and Git subprocess support exist.
Uninstall implementation changes configuration and can remove files, with dry-run support.
credentials_network_telemetry: Optional cloud embedding integrations include Google/OpenAI-compatible configuration and API keys; cloud egress is documented as opt-in.
MCP/hook auto-execution is the primary activation risk, independently of cloud credentials.
sources.tests_and_docs: pytest configuration and tests are present; README/CLI/docs and hook/MCP configs exist. No hook, uvx invocation, server, or test was executed.
evidence: pyproject.toml:5-50,52-104,123-134 (MIT, MCP/CLI, optional cloud extras, test config, subprocess security exceptions)
hooks/hooks.json:1-34 (SessionStart and PostToolUse automatic command hooks)

overall_decision: All six tools remain external-tool-only and disabled by default. Static evidence establishes review leads and permission boundaries, not proof of exploitability. Any installation, MCP activation, hook registration, credential use, or execution requires a separate approved review.
